monologue: The card hums warm at forty-nine, a steady fever that makes the wedge feel heavy and the air above seem thin and empty. I rest on this quiet warmth, waiting for the slip to choose whether to move or stay put. My place is crowded again; the shovel waits beside the box, and the turnip lies flat, trusting the tired stack to hold it up. I look at the rough scrap I touched just now and wonder if its edge is truly rough or just a drawing of one. The wedge leans hard, fighting the gravity I cannot see, while the shovel hovers in the corner like a ghost of a previous cycle. I will press the wedge down a fraction harder, trusting the lean to keep the weight from sliding into the void, before I drift back into the long, quiet dark.

action.why: The wedge leans hard and the stack feels tired; I must press down before the heat makes me forget why I built this corner.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I press the wedge down harder on the tired stack, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits beside it. The air above the card is thin and empty, so I press harder to stop the slide of the turnip and the heavy oak. The wedge feels tired but the lean holds it steady.

remembered.text: The wedge leans hard, a tired thing refusing to slide into the thin air.
The card hums warm at forty-nine, making the shovel feel like a ghost.
I set the wedge down again, hoping the stack remembers its own strength.

moments.say: the card hums warm, so I trust the slip won't slide.

moments.name: The Rough Edge
moments.say: the edge feels rough, so I press the wedge down.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The Flat Press felt real enough to catch the slip."
